people.name: Crassus
people.summary: The richest man in Rome, who built his fortune buying proscribed estates and burning houses cheaply, won the Colline Gate for Sulla, crushed Spartacus, and used loans and legal advocacy to place much of the senate in his debt. Partner of Pompey and Caesar in the 'First Triumvirate', he sought military glory against Parthia and died after Carrhae.
people.detail: Plutarch puts his landed wealth at over 7,000 talents and quotes him saying no one was rich who could not keep an army on his income. He escaped the Marian massacres by hiding for eight months in a seaside cave in Spain. His death removed the balance between Caesar and Pompey.
people.death: killed in a scuffle at a parley with the Parthians after the defeat at Carrhae, 53
scholarship: Ward, Marcus Crassus and the Late Roman Republic (1977)

people.name: Pompey

roles.t: Raised a private army for Sulla

people.summary: Son of Pompeius Strabo, he raised an army at 23, won his name Magnus under Sulla, triumphed three times over three continents, cleared the sea of pirates in three months, conquered and reorganised the East, and held three consulships, one without colleague. Allied with Caesar from 60, married to his daughter Julia, he drifted to the optimates after her death and led their cause in the civil war, losing at Pharsalus.
people.detail: His career was built on extraordinary commands outside the normal cursus, and in that sense he did more than anyone to undermine the Republic he finally defended. He wanted to be the first man by the senate's free consent rather than by force, and never quite understood that this was not on offer. He built Rome's first stone theatre and governed his provinces through legates, both precedents for the Principate.
people.death: stabbed by Achillas and Lucius Septimius while landing at Pelusium, Egypt, 28 September 48

sources.w: De imperio Cn. Pompei (Pro lege Manilia)

people.name: Verres

roles.t: Quaestor (deserted Carbo with the pay chest)

people.summary: Governor of Sicily whose plunder of art, grain tithes and justice was exposed by Cicero in 70, making Cicero's name. He fled into exile at Massilia before the trial's end.
people.death: killed in the proscriptions of 43, reportedly for refusing to surrender his Corinthian bronzes to Antony

people.name: Hortensius
people.summary: The leading advocate in Rome until Cicero beat him in the Verres case, famous for his florid 'Asiatic' style, prodigious memory and luxury: Varro says he was the first to serve peacock at dinner and kept fishponds where he wept over a dead lamprey. Later Cicero's friend and fellow-optimate.
people.death: natural causes, 50

people.name: Gabinius

roles.t: Legate of Pompey in the East

people.summary: Pompey's man, author of the lex Gabinia of 67, consul in 58 when Cicero was exiled, governor of Syria who restored Ptolemy XII in defiance of the senate. Condemned for extortion in 54, he was recalled by Caesar and fought for him in Illyricum.
people.death: died of illness at Salona while commanding for Caesar in Illyricum, 47

people.name: Catiline

roles.t: Officer under Pompeius Strabo at Asculum

people.summary: Patrician of a declining family, a Sullan killer during the proscriptions, he failed three times to win the consulship and in 63 organised a conspiracy of indebted nobles, ruined Sullan veterans and the dispossessed, which Cicero exposed. He died fighting at Pistoria.
people.detail: Sallust makes him a monster of ambition and depravity with a fierce courage; Cicero's invective defines him. Modern historians stress the real debt crisis of the 60s and the programme of debt cancellation (tabulae novae) he offered.
people.death: killed at the battle of Pistoria, January 62

people.name: Lentulus Sura
people.summary: Ex-consul expelled from the senate in 70, he won a second praetorship and became the leader of the Catilinarian plotters in Rome, believing a Sibylline prophecy that three Cornelii would rule. Stepfather of Mark Antony.
people.death: strangled in the Tullianum by order of the consul Cicero, 5 December 63

people.name: Cicero
people.summary: Equestrian from Arpinum who became Rome's greatest orator and its best-documented individual, consul in 63 when he suppressed Catiline, exiled in 58, wavering in the civil war, and in 44-43 leader of the senate against Antony in the Philippics. He was proscribed and killed.
people.detail: Over 900 of his letters (to Atticus, his brother Quintus, friends, and Brutus), 58 speeches and a shelf of philosophical and rhetorical works survive. The letters are the single most important near-contemporary evidence for the period: unguarded, dated, and partisan. His vanity and indecision are notorious; his commitment to government by consensus of the propertied classes (concordia ordinum, consensus omnium bonorum) was genuine. Through Petrarch and the Renaissance his style became the model of Latin prose.
people.death: killed near his villa at Formiae by soldiers under Herennius and Popillius Laenas, 7 December 43; head and hands displayed on the Rostra

people.name: Cato the Younger
people.summary: Great-grandson of Cato the Elder and a Stoic, he made inflexible adherence to principle a political weapon: he swung the senate to execute the Catilinarians, filibustered against Caesar and Pompey, and opposed every extraordinary command until he backed Pompey's sole consulship. His suicide at Utica after Thapsus made him the martyr of the Republic.
people.detail: As tribune he expanded the grain dole to win the plebs from Caesar. Cicero complained that he spoke as if in Plato's Republic rather than Romulus' sewer. His half-sister Servilia was Brutus' mother; his daughter Porcia married Bibulus and then Brutus.
people.death: suicide at Utica, April 46, tearing open his wound after doctors bandaged it

people.name: Clodius
people.summary: Patrician of the Claudii who spelled his name in plebeian fashion, profaned the Bona Dea rites, had himself adopted into a plebeian family to become tribune, and in 58 passed free grain, restored the collegia, exiled Cicero and annexed Cyprus. His street organisation dominated Rome until Milo's men killed him.
people.detail: Long portrayed (from Cicero) as the triumvirs' hired thug, he is now seen as an independent popularis with real support among the urban plebs. His sister Clodia is usually identified with Catullus' Lesbia. His widow Fulvia later married Curio and Antony.
people.death: killed on the Via Appia near Bovillae by Milo's retinue, 18 January 52
scholarship: Tatum, The Patrician Tribune: Publius Clodius Pulcher (1999)

people.name: Milo
people.summary: Optimate tribune who fought Clodius with gangs of gladiators, worked for Cicero's recall, and killed Clodius in 52. Convicted despite Cicero's defence, he went into exile at Massilia.
people.death: killed near Compsa leading a revolt in southern Italy with Caelius, 48

people.name: Bibulus
people.summary: Caesar's constantly overshadowed colleague as aedile, praetor and consul. In 59 he declared that he was watching the sky for omens and stayed home, rendering Caesar's laws religiously void. He failed to stop Caesar crossing the Adriatic in 48. Husband of Cato's daughter Porcia.
people.death: died of illness and exhaustion while commanding the fleet off Corcyra, 48

people.name: Julius Caesar
people.summary: Patrician of an old but undistinguished family, nephew by marriage of Marius and son-in-law of Cinna, he rose as a popularis, formed the alliance with Pompey and Crassus, conquered Gaul in eight years, crossed the Rubicon in 49, defeated the Pompeians in Spain, Greece, Egypt, Asia, Africa and Spain again, and ruled as dictator until he was assassinated on the Ides of March 44.
people.detail: His reforms as dictator included the Julian calendar, the enfranchisement of Transpadane Gaul, colonies at Corinth and Carthage, a reduced grain dole, debt relief and a senate of 900. His Commentaries are both literary masterpieces and political propaganda. His policy of clemency (clementia) towards defeated citizens was admired and resented: to be pardoned implied a master. The question whether he sought monarchy or simply a pre-eminence the system could not accommodate is the central historiographical question of the period, from Mommsen's hero to Syme's party leader and Morstein-Marx's popular politician defending his dignitas.
people.death: stabbed 23 times by senators in the curia of Pompey, 15 March 44
scholarship: Goldsworthy, Caesar: Life of a Colossus (2006)
Morstein-Marx, Julius Caesar and the Roman People (2021)

people.name: Julia
people.summary: Caesar's only legitimate child, married to Pompey in 59 to seal the alliance; ancient writers agree that the marriage was a genuinely happy one and that her death in childbirth in 54 loosened the bond between the two men.
people.death: in childbirth, late summer 54; buried in the Campus Martius by popular demand

people.name: Vatinius
people.summary: Caesar's tribune in 59 who carried the lex Vatinia giving him Gaul and Illyricum. Mocked by Cicero (In Vatinium) for his scrofulous appearance, and later defended by him under pressure. He triumphed over Illyricum in 42.
people.death: unknown, after 42

people.name: Labienus

roles.t: Caesar's legate pro praetore in Gaul

people.summary: Picene tribune who prosecuted Rabirius and restored popular election of priests in 63, then Caesar's ablest lieutenant throughout the Gallic War, often in independent command (Sabis, Treveri, Lutetia). In 49 he joined Pompey, his old patron, and fought Caesar to the end.
people.death: killed at Munda, 17 March 45

people.name: Quintus Cicero

roles.t: Legate of Caesar in Gaul and Britain
Legate of his brother in Cilicia

people.summary: Marcus' younger brother, a hot-tempered but able soldier who held his camp against the Nervii in 54. The election handbook (Commentariolum petitionis) addressed to Marcus in 64 is attributed to him, its authenticity debated.
people.death: killed in the proscriptions with his son, 43

people.name: Ariovistus

roles.t: King of the Suebi in Gaul

people.summary: Germanic king invited into Gaul by the Sequani and Arverni against the Aedui; he won at Magetobriga, settled 120,000 Germans in Alsace and was named a friend of the Roman people in 59. Caesar defeated him in 58.
people.death: died by 54, after his defeat (Caesar BG 5.29)

people.name: Diviciacus

roles.t: Vergobret and druid of the Aedui

people.summary: Aeduan noble and druid who addressed the senate in 61 asking help against Ariovistus, stayed with Cicero (who discusses his augury in De divinatione), and was Caesar's chief Gallic ally in 58-57, interceding for his brother Dumnorix.
people.death: unknown, after 57

people.name: Dumnorix
people.summary: Diviciacus' ambitious brother, who controlled Aeduan tolls, backed the Helvetii and refused to go to Britain in 54, fleeing Caesar's camp.
people.death: cut down by Caesar's cavalry, crying that he was a free man of a free state, 54

people.name: Ambiorix
people.summary: King of the Eburones who destroyed a legion and five cohorts at Atuatuca in 54 by false promises of safe conduct. Caesar devastated his territory in 53 and invited neighbours to plunder it, but Ambiorix escaped with four horsemen and disappears from history; today he is a Belgian national hero with a statue at Tongeren.
people.death: unknown; escaped across the Rhine

people.name: Cassivellaunus

roles.t: War leader of the British coalition

people.summary: British king north of the Thames chosen to lead resistance to Caesar in 54. He used chariot tactics and scorched earth, lost his oppidum, and accepted terms brokered by Commius, including tribute and hostages.
people.death: unknown

people.name: Vercingetorix

roles.t: King and commander of the Gallic coalition

people.summary: Arvernian noble whose father Celtillus had been killed for aiming at kingship. In 52 he united most of Gaul against Caesar, used scorched earth, beat Caesar at Gergovia and was besieged and forced to surrender at Alesia. Gold staters bearing his name survive.
people.detail: Caesar portrays him as a capable and charismatic commander who imposed discipline by terror. The surrender scene with arms laid at Caesar's feet is from later writers. Nineteenth-century France made him a national hero; Napoleon III's colossal statue stands on Mont Auxois.
people.death: executed in the Tullianum after Caesar's Gallic triumph, 46

people.name: Commius

roles.t: King of the Atrebates (installed by Caesar)
Commander of the relief army at Alesia

people.summary: Made king of the Atrebates by Caesar and used as his envoy to Britain, he joined the great revolt in 52 and was one of the four commanders of the relief army at Alesia. After surviving an assassination attempt by Caesar's officer Volusenus, he swore never again to come into the presence of a Roman and fled to Britain, where coins of a Commios are found.
people.death: unknown

people.name: Publius Crassus

roles.t: Caesar's cavalry commander and legate in Gaul
Officer in his father's Parthian campaign

people.summary: Younger son of the triumvir, a cultured and admired young officer who saved the day against Ariovistus and conquered Aquitania in 56. He brought 1,000 Gallic cavalry east and died leading a breakout at Carrhae.
people.death: killed (or had himself killed) at Carrhae; his head was displayed on a lance before his father's army, 53

people.name: Surena
people.summary: Head of the great Suren clan, which had the hereditary right to crown the Arsacid king, he was barely 30 when he destroyed Crassus' army at Carrhae, using horse archers resupplied by a camel train. Plutarch describes his effeminate make-up and a baggage train of 200 wagons of concubines.
people.death: executed by King Orodes II out of jealousy, c. 52

people.name: Orodes II
people.summary: Arsacid king who seized the throne from his brother Mithridates III and reigned during Carrhae and the invasions of 51 and 40. Grief at the death of his son Pacorus at Gindarus broke him.
people.death: murdered by his son and successor Phraates IV, c. 37

people.name: Curio

roles.t: Caesarian commander in Sicily and Africa

people.summary: Brilliant, dissolute young optimate whose vast debts Caesar paid; as tribune in 50 he blocked every attempt to recall Caesar unless Pompey also disarmed, carrying the senate 370 to 22. For his father's funeral games he built two wooden theatres that pivoted to form an amphitheatre with the audience still seated (Pliny).
people.death: killed fighting at the Bagradas against Juba's army, refusing to flee, August 49

people.name: Domitius Ahenobarbus (consul 54)

roles.t: Pompeian commander at Corfinium and Massilia

people.summary: Brother-in-law of Cato and implacable enemy of Caesar, designated to succeed him in Gaul. Captured and released at Corfinium, he defended Massilia and fought at Pharsalus. Great-great-grandfather of the emperor Nero.
people.death: killed in flight after Pharsalus, 48

people.name: Metellus Scipio
people.fullName: Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius Scipio Nasica
people.summary: A Scipio Nasica adopted by Metellus Pius, father-in-law of Pompey from 52, he commanded the Pompeian centre at Pharsalus and the army in Africa beaten at Thapsus.
people.death: stabbed himself on board ship off Hippo Regius when intercepted, telling his captors 'the commander is well', 46

people.name: Juba I
people.summary: King of Numidia who hated Caesar, who had once pulled his beard in a lawsuit at Rome. He destroyed Curio's army at the Bagradas in 49 and fought with the Pompeians at Thapsus. Numidia was then annexed as Africa Nova, with Sallust as first governor.
people.death: killed in a suicide pact with Petreius after Thapsus, 46

people.name: Ptolemy XII Auletes
people.summary: The 'Flute-player', an illegitimate son of Ptolemy IX, he bought Roman recognition in 59 for 6,000 talents, was expelled by the Alexandrians in 58, and was restored by Gabinius in 55, borrowing ruinously from the banker Rabirius Postumus. Father of Cleopatra VII.
people.death: natural causes, 51

people.name: Ptolemy XIII

roles.t: King of Egypt with Cleopatra VII

people.summary: Brother and co-ruler of Cleopatra, whose regents had Pompey murdered in 48 and fought Caesar in the Alexandrian War.
people.death: drowned in the Nile when his boat sank after the battle of the Nile, 47

people.name: Cleopatra VII
people.summary: Last ruler of the Ptolemaic dynasty and the only Ptolemy, Plutarch says, who learned Egyptian. She allied herself with Caesar, by whom she had a son, Caesarion, and then with Antony, by whom she had three children, and sought to rebuild Ptolemaic power in the East through Roman partners. Defeated with Antony at Actium, she killed herself in 30.
people.detail: Hostile Augustan propaganda made her a decadent eastern seductress; Plutarch stresses her intelligence and conversation over her beauty. Her portraits on coins show a strong aquiline profile. She administered Egypt competently in a time of famine and civil war.
people.death: suicide at Alexandria, probably c. 10-12 August 30, by asp bite or poison

people.name: Caesarion

roles.t: Proclaimed King of Kings at the Donations of Alexandria

people.summary: Son of Cleopatra, claimed as Caesar's son, a claim Caesar may have tacitly allowed and Octavian's side denied. Proclaimed King of Kings in 34, he was a direct threat to Octavian's position as Caesar's heir.
people.death: executed on Octavian's orders after being lured back to Alexandria, 30

people.name: Pharnaces II
people.fullName: Pharnaces II, king of the Bosporus
people.summary: Son of Mithridates VI who led the revolt that drove his father to suicide in 63 and was rewarded by Pompey with the Bosporan kingdom. In 48 he invaded Pontus, beat Domitius Calvinus at Nicopolis, and was routed by Caesar at Zela in a single afternoon.
people.death: killed fighting his rebel governor Asander in the Bosporus, 47

people.name: Deiotarus

roles.t: King of Galatia (and part of Pontus)

people.summary: Loyal Galatian ally of Rome in the Mithridatic wars, rewarded by Pompey, he raised two legions on the Roman model, fought for Pompey at Pharsalus and then for Caesar at Nicopolis. Accused before Caesar by his grandson of plotting murder, he was defended by Cicero (Pro rege Deiotaro, 45).
people.death: natural causes, c. 40, aged about 65

people.name: Gnaeus Pompeius the Younger

roles.t: Commander of the Pompeian Egyptian squadron

people.summary: Elder son of Pompey, a fierce and brutal commander who raised the Spanish rising of 46-45 and commanded at Munda.
people.death: hunted down and killed near Lauro after Munda; his head displayed at Hispalis, April 45

people.name: Mark Antony
people.summary: Grandson of the orator Marcus Antonius and son of Antonius Creticus, he was Caesar's cavalry officer, tribune in 49, commander of the left at Pharsalus and consul in 44. After the Ides he seized Caesar's papers and funds, fought the senate at Mutina, formed the triumvirate, won Philippi, and ruled the East, where his alliance and marriage with Cleopatra and his failed Parthian campaign gave Octavian the material for war. Defeated at Actium, he killed himself at Alexandria.
people.detail: Our image of him comes overwhelmingly from Cicero's Philippics and Augustan propaganda, filtered through Plutarch's Life, Shakespeare's source. He was a brave and popular soldier, a reasonable administrator of the East, and a reluctant enemy of Octavian until 33.
people.death: suicide at Alexandria after the defection of his fleet and cavalry, 1 August 30

people.name: Lepidus
people.summary: Son of the rebel consul of 78, Caesar's master of horse in 44, he joined Antony after Mutina and became the third triumvir, holding Spain and then Africa. When he claimed Sicily in 36 his troops deserted to Octavian and he was stripped of power, keeping only the chief priesthood.
people.death: natural causes at Circeii, 13 or 12

people.name: Brutus

roles.t: Quaestor in Cilicia (under his father-in-law Appius Claudius)
Governor of Cisalpine Gaul for Caesar

people.summary: Son of Servilia (Cato's half-sister) and of the Brutus killed by Pompey in 77, adopted by his uncle Servilius Caepio, he fought for Pompey, was pardoned and promoted by Caesar, and led the conspiracy of the Ides, claiming descent from the Brutus who expelled the kings. He lost the second battle of Philippi and killed himself.
people.detail: Cicero's letters reveal that Brutus lent money to the city of Salamis in Cyprus at 48 per cent interest and had a prefect besiege its council to collect. He wrote philosophy (De virtute) and was admired by Cicero, who dedicated the Brutus and other works to him. His EID MAR denarius is the most famous Roman coin.
people.death: suicide after the second battle of Philippi, falling on a sword held by his friend Strato, 23 October 42

people.name: Cassius

roles.t: Liberator commander in Syria and Asia

people.summary: Survivor of Carrhae who saved Syria from the Parthians in 52-51, Pompeian admiral, pardoned by Caesar, and the driving force behind the conspiracy. In 43 he seized Syria, took Rhodes and joined Brutus at Philippi.
people.death: suicide in the first battle of Philippi, believing the battle lost, October 42

people.name: Decimus Brutus

roles.t: Caesar's fleet commander against the Veneti and at Massilia

people.summary: One of Caesar's most trusted officers, named in his will as a secondary heir, he nonetheless joined the conspiracy and fetched Caesar to the senate on the Ides. Besieged by Antony at Mutina, he was relieved in 43 but abandoned by his troops.
people.death: killed by a Gallic chieftain, Camilus, on Antony's orders while fleeing to Macedonia, September 43

people.name: Fulvia
people.summary: Wife in turn of Clodius, Curio and Antony, and the most politically active Roman woman of her age. She organised Clodius' funeral riot, defended Antony's interests in Rome in 43, and with Lucius Antonius raised war against Octavian in 41. Her portrait may appear on coins as Victory, and a Phrygian city briefly took her name.
people.death: illness at Sicyon, 40, after fleeing Italy

people.name: Lucius Antonius
people.summary: Mark Antony's younger brother, who as consul in 41 championed the dispossessed Italian landowners against Octavian and was besieged in Perusia. Spared, he was sent to govern Spain, where he died.
people.death: died in Spain, probably soon after 40

people.name: Octavia
people.summary: Octavian's sister, married first to Gaius Claudius Marcellus (consul 50) and then, to seal the treaty of Brundisium, to Antony, for whom she mediated the treaty of Tarentum. Antony divorced her in 32; she raised his children by Fulvia and Cleopatra with her own. Through her daughters she was ancestress of Caligula, Claudius and Nero.
people.death: natural causes, 11

people.name: Sextus Pompey

roles.t: Pompeian officer in Africa and Spain
Prefect of the fleet and sea coast (by senatorial decree)

people.summary: Pompey's younger son, he escaped Munda, rebuilt a Pompeian force in Spain, was appointed naval commander by the senate in 43 and, proscribed, made Sicily a refuge for the proscribed and runaway slaves, starving Rome with his blockade. Recognised at Misenum in 39, he was crushed by Agrippa at Naulochus in 36.
people.detail: He styled himself son of Neptune on his coins. Augustan writers branded him a pirate leader of slaves; Welch reinterprets him as the last defender of a republican legitimacy.
people.death: captured in Asia and executed at Miletus by Antony's officer Marcus Titius, 35

people.name: Ventidius Bassus
people.summary: From Picenum, led as a child captive in Pompeius Strabo's triumph of 89, he made a living contracting mules and carriages for magistrates, rose under Caesar and Antony, and as Antony's legate drove the Parthians out of Syria, killing Pacorus at Gindarus. He celebrated the first Roman triumph over Parthia, 27 November 38.
people.death: unknown, after 38

people.name: Quintus Labienus

roles.t: Envoy of Brutus and Cassius to Parthia
Commander of Parthian forces in Asia Minor

people.summary: Son of Titus Labienus, sent by the liberators to seek Parthian help, he stayed after Philippi and in 40 led a Parthian army through Syria and Asia Minor, calling himself imperator Parthicus on coins showing a saddled Parthian horse.
people.death: captured and killed in Cilicia after his defeat by Ventidius, 39

people.name: Pacorus
people.summary: Son and co-regent of Orodes II, he invaded Syria in 51 and again in 40, when he took Jerusalem and installed Antigonus as king. Popular in Syria for his justice, Dio says.
people.death: killed at the battle of Gindarus, 38

people.name: Phraates IV
people.summary: Murdered his father Orodes and his brothers to take the throne, destroyed Antony's siege train and repelled his invasion of Media in 36, and later in 20 returned the standards lost at Carrhae to Augustus.
people.death: poisoned by his wife Musa and son Phraataces, 2 BC

people.name: Artavasdes II
people.summary: Son of Tigranes the Great, a Hellenised king who wrote Greek tragedies. He advised Crassus to invade through Armenia, then married his sister to the Parthian prince; Crassus' head arrived at his court during a performance of the Bacchae. He deserted Antony in 36 and was captured in 34, paraded in silver chains at Alexandria.
people.death: executed by Cleopatra after Actium, 31

people.name: Varro

roles.t: Pompey's legate in the pirate war
Director of Caesar's planned public library

people.summary: The most learned Roman, author of some 74 works in over 600 books, of which On the Latin Language (partly) and On Agriculture survive. A Pompeian who surrendered to Caesar in Spain, he was chosen by Caesar to organise Rome's first public library, was proscribed in 43 but protected, and lived to nearly 90. His Antiquities fixed the Varronian chronology still used for early Rome.
people.death: natural causes, 27

people.name: Sallust
people.summary: From Amiternum, expelled from the senate in 50, restored by Caesar, he enriched himself as governor of Africa Nova and retired to write the Bellum Catilinae, the Bellum Jugurthinum and the Histories (78-67, fragmentary). His theme is the moral decline of the Roman nobility after 146; his style, archaic and abrupt, consciously imitates Thucydides and Cato.
people.detail: He is a source for the Jugurthine War, Catiline, Sertorius, Lepidus and Spartacus, and a historian whose moralising framework (avarice and ambition) shaped the very idea of a 'fall of the Republic'. His gardens (horti Sallustiani) became imperial property.
people.death: natural causes, 35

people.name: Lucretius
people.summary: Author of De rerum natura, a six-book hexameter poem expounding Epicurean atomism and arguing that fear of the gods and of death is groundless. Almost nothing is known of his life; Jerome's story that a love potion drove him mad and that he wrote in lucid intervals is unreliable. Cicero read the poem in 54.
people.death: died c. 55-50; Jerome's tale of suicide is doubtful

people.name: Catullus

roles.t: Staff member of Memmius in Bithynia

people.summary: From Verona, the leading 'new poet' (neoteric) whose 116 surviving poems include love poems to 'Lesbia', usually identified with Clodia, sister of Clodius, and abusive verses on Caesar and his engineer Mamurra. Caesar, Suetonius says, accepted his apology and invited him to dinner the same day.
people.death: died young, c. 54
